operational_flag.verdict: DAYTIME CADENCE HEALTHY, NIGHTLY BLACKOUT NOW THREE FOR THREE
operational_flag.coverage_24h: 75 state-file commits in the 24h to 2026-07-31 14:14Z against ~72 expected (104%), median gap 13.2 min.
operational_flag.pattern: THIRD consecutive night in the same window: 367 min (07-28 21:40Z -> 07-29 03:47Z), 368 min (07-29 21:58Z -> 07-30 04:05Z), 357 min (07-30 21:40Z -> 07-31 03:37Z). Three near-identical durations starting within 18 minutes of each other is systematic, not throttling, and matches the previously diagnosed mechanism: bot.yml runs a ~5h45m self-looping job under concurrency with cancel-in-progress:false, so the successor sits queued behind the lock. The owner's pre-agreed escalation to an external trigger, scoped to the 21:40Z-03:40Z handoff, is now warranted on three data points.
operational_flag.misleading_signal: A raw data/ commit at 2026-07-31 03:10Z appears to break the gap but is NOT a cycle - it is the owner's manual v2-review push (71b8a6c). The first automated cycle after the blackout was 03:37:00Z (f270149). Measuring the gap from the 03:10Z commit understates it by 27 minutes.
operational_flag.secondary_gap: 42.6 min, 2026-07-31 09:20Z -> 10:02Z. Under the 90-minute threshold; noted for trend only.
operational_flag.failed_runs: 0 failures. 3 runs concluded 'cancelled' in the window (07-30 20:23Z, 07-30 23:45Z, 07-31 03:11Z), consistent with the 355-minute timeout cap firing at the end of the 345-minute internal loop plus the owner's push interrupting the 03:11Z run. INFERRED, not confirmed.
operational_flag.gh_run_list_caveat: STILL APPLIES and bit again this run: 'gh run list' without a workflow filter is dominated by pages-build-deployment runs. 'gh run list --workflow bot.yml' returns EMPTY (the filter wants the workflow NAME, paper-trade-cycle, not the filename), so gaps must be computed from data/ commit timestamps. Both wrong methods read as healthier than the truth.
